messages.author: 1cd3ce37d8489fec
messages.subject: Constraints on ordered vectors?
parts:
Hi,

I have a question about constraining ordered vectors that is hopefully not just a typo on my part! (But probably is just that.)

I am getting the following parser error:



 35:    parameters {
...
 37:            ordered<lower=x_min, upper=x_max>[K] x_offset;
                  ^
 38:    

PARSER EXPECTED: "["



The code compiles and runs when I remove the constraint.

Is this not the expected syntax for declaring constraints on ordered vectors?  I'm looking at e.g. the thread below as an example.

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/stan-users/aN6eFv7Qmo8

I'm using pystan 2.7.0.0.

Thanks in advance for any advice!

Best,

~Nathan

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Constraints on ordered vectors?
parts:
On Friday, September 4, 2015 at 5:48:12 PM UTC-4, N Sanders wrote:
I am getting the following parser error:

 35:    parameters {
...
 37:            ordered<lower=x_min, upper=x_max>[K] x_offset;
                  ^
 38:

ordered cannot be further constrained in the declaration. You could transform each element to the (x_min,x_max) interval manually with an inverse logit transformation or something but don't forget about the Jacobian term (which is just the sum of log partial derivatives in this case).

Ben
